payload.name: Search event memories for monetized passions
payload.description: When a question asks what someone loves and can make money from (earn, monetize, income, prize), also search event memories with concrete earning/competition terms before answering.
content: When a question asks what a person loves or enjoys and can make money from (e.g., monetize, earn, income, prize), do not restrict memory kinds to preference/state; run an additional search over memory_kind=event using concrete terms such as 'tournament', 'competition', 'won', 'prize', 'earned', 'paid', 'income' for that person.

If an event memory describes a win or a paid activity connected to a passion, treat it as direct evidence even when the question is phrased in terms of likes or loves; inspect the newest version of each returned memory before answering.
Do not answer from preference restatements of behavior alone when event memories about earnings may exist; run the event-kind search before concluding evidence is insufficient.

solves: Questions pairing enjoyment with monetization were answered only from preference/state memories although the decisive evidence was an enriched event memory of winning and earning. The mechanism is restricting retrieval to subjective kinds and omitting income/competition terms. Future questions joining love and money should include event-kind searches with won, prize, earned, paid, tournament; not enjoyment-only questions.
